training_data: Cohort 1, Department of Neurology, Second Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University (22 AD / 19 MCI / 19 CN): metabolite selection (OPLS-DA, RF, SVM, Boruta) and GB/LR/RF diagnostic models
test_data: Independent cohort 2 (20 AD / 20 MCI / 20 CN), recruited by the same hospital team under the same ethics approval
reason: Cohort 2 is a separately recruited sample from the same institution: the only ethics committee and the only clinical team named belong to the Second Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University. That is a same-institution validation cohort, which the audit excludes from V4. V3 stands because the 10- and 13-metabolite panels chosen in cohort 1 were scored in cohort 2. The paper does not say whether the cohort-2 GB/RF models were the cohort-1 models applied unchanged or were refitted (the metabolite+MMSE models reported in cohort 2 have no cohort-1 counterpart), hence null for the fixed-model field.

quotes.quote: The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of the Clinical Research Center of the Second Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University and all participants signed informed consent forms for the study. Two cohorts were enrolled in this study, Cohort 1 included 22 patients diagnosed with AD, 19 patients diagnosed with MCI and 19 CN.

The biomarkers were then validated using GB, LR and RF in cohort 1. Furthermore, the biomarkers in AD and MCI were both validated using GB and RF in the validation cohort 2 and the metabolite panel performance was compared with MMSE scale.
In addition, diagnostic markers identified in cohort 1 were further confirmed in the validation cohort, by comparing the ROC analysis of metabolites and MMSE in both AD and MCI groups.
YM, HM, ZC and YL conducted the clinical study and sample collection.
